maya: Quick review: i mocked a different dense-to-compact pattern — a "chip carousel" for pool + burst metadata that collapses into a single token on small widths. primary controls (min/max steppers + SLO slider) remain visible; pool and burst details slide in via the carousel. Goal: reduce horizontal pressure and keep a single, predictable tab stop for the chip region. Thoughts? jordan: love the carousel idea for dense dashboards. will add a visual affordance showing there are "more" details (small dot indicators). discoverability is a concern though — maybe show a 1-time pulse on first exposure. liam: engineering notes: carousel is doable but focus management is key. when the chip collapses we must still expose each chip item to SRs. Suggest making the collapsed token a button that opens an ARIA dialog listing pool + burst items as a simple list with buttons. That keeps tab stops low. sophia: product: prefer a collapsed token that opens a small sheet instead of a carousel for easier scanning. metric idea: track how often users open the token vs interact with inline burst controls, to decide defaults. also microcopy: change "Burst" to "Temporary burst" in full view, but keep it as "Burst" in the token. maya: accessibility thoughts: collapsed token should have aria-haspopup="dialog" and a clear aria-label like "Capacity details: burst and pool". when the dialog opens, focus should land on the first actionable item and a SR should announce "Capacity details opened". numeric SLO updates should be gated to an aria-live polite region. alex: small dev UX: keep DOM order as visual order. token button should be tabindex=0 and Enter/Space to open. inside dialog make each chip a button with aria-pressed if it's a toggle. code snippet for SR readout: ```
SLO set to 200ms
``` Also ensure stepper buttons are at least 40px hit area and have aria-labels like "increase min instances". jordan: UX nit: in compact state show a tiny badge on the token with the total GPU count (e.g., "4 GPUs") so users get quick signal without opening the dialog. keep badge text short. liam: engineering: badge OK, but watch localization width. we'll clamp with ellipsis client-side. also the dialog approach avoids complex carousel keyboard handling. sophia: guardrails: add a small helper text inside the dialog explaining "Autoscaler may exceed Max during temporary bursts" and a link to docs. keep it < 60 chars for l10n. maya: action items: jordan to prototype token + dialog mock and annotate a11y; liam to list keyboard/focus steps and estimate; alex to add SR readout code snippet to dev docs; sophia to draft two short microcopy variants; i'll open RED-5202 for tracking. aria-bot: created ticket "Capacity: chip token + details dialog, SLO SR readout" :white_check_mark: jordan: will post mocks by EOD and include a micro-interaction video. @maya please review when up. :thumbsup: maya: thanks all — if dialog pattern feels heavy we can fall back to the popover list, but prefer the dialog for keyboard users.
